subject: Request: annotated isolation & topology package for SOC 2 / SIG review
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <security@acmeinc.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data isolation and network topology for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for taking our security review. As part of our SIG and SOC 2 evidence pack we need: a concise architecture overview for Dedicated and Private deployments that highlights network and control-plane isolation, annotated diagrams showing the data plane separation (inference runtime vs control plane), and a CAIQ/SIG crosswalk for the controls that map to network/isolation requirements.

Can you provide:
- An annotated topology diagram we can include in our audit binder
- A short narrative (1–2 pages) describing tenant fencing, KMS boundaries, and egress controls
- A completed SIG/CAIQ crosswalk spreadsheet focused on network/isolation controls

Target delivery: Dec 29 (we need to include it in our January attestation packet). If there are any limitations (e.g., redacted IPs, non-disclosure items), call them out.

Appreciate it —
Laura Bennett
Information Security Lead, Acme Financial
security@acmeinc.com

Attachments: N/A

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data isolation and network topology for SOC 2 / SIG review

Looks good — quick checklist for the deliverable so we stay audit-ready:

1) Diagram requirements (Marissa):
- One page high-level topology for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (annotate: control plane, data plane, KV cache boundaries, network ACLs, peering/APE, edge termination)
- A second page with a simplified reachability matrix (component -> allowed egress destinations, ports/protocols)
- Redact internal IPs; include example ranges where helpful and call out exceptions (e.g., on-prem airgapped customer requiring offline transfer)

2) Narrative (Marissa / Grace):
- Tenant fencing description (how we enforce per-customer isolation at the runtime and network layers)
- KMS/HSM boundaries and key access model (who can request key material, rotation cadence)
- Egress control policy (how we defend-exfiltration, egress NAT, proxying, logging)

3) SIG/CAIQ crosswalk (Karthik):
- Populate network isolation controls (NET-*, IDF-*) and include evidence refs (diagram page, syslog examples, config snippets).

4) Attestation language (Kimberly):
- Short statement we can sign for SOC 2 that the architecture supports the described controls; note any control exceptions or customer-managed components.

Marissa — can you deliver draft diagrams by Monday (12/20) so Karthik has time to map controls? Ben — if there are contractual disclosure limits, flag them.

-Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data isolation and network topology for SOC 2 / SIG review

Folks — picking this up. Drafts attached:
- redwood-dedicated-private-isolation-diagram_v1.png (high-level + annotated callouts)
- controlplane-dataflow-annotated.pdf (1-page narrative + flow labels)

Notes:
- I created two variants of the topology: Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pool with Redwood-managed control plane in our VPC) and Private (customer-managed control plane in their VPC with our runtime in an air-gapped environment).
- For Dedicated we show cross-account VPC peering with strict route tables and an egress NAT gateway per tenant pool. For Private we highlight optional on-prem provisioning and show a proxy-airlock transfer process.
- I redacted exact CIDR blocks but included pseudoranges (10.0.0.0/16 style) to satisfy architecture reviewers.

Question: do we need a signed statement about encryption-at-rest keys being in a customer-managed KMS for Private deployments? If so Kimberly — can you draft a short attestation I can include?

-Marissa
Sr. Cloud Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-private-isolation-diagram_v1.png, controlplane-dataflow-annotated.pdf

Subject: Re: Deliverable: annotated isolation & topology package for SOC 2 / SIG review

Hi Laura —

Attached is the package we discussed for the SOC 2/SIG review:
- redwood-dedicated-private-isolation-diagram_v3.png (finalized topology diagram; redacted CIDRs but annotated reachability)
- controlplane-dataflow-annotated.pdf (1.5 page narrative describing tenant fencing, KMS/HSM boundaries, egress controls and logical flow)
- sig-caaiq-crosswalk_ACME.xlsx (SIG/CAIQ crosswalk with references to diagram pages and config artifacts)

A few important notes:
- For Private (customer-hosted control plane) the customer is responsible for KMS custody if they elect customer-managed KMS; we call that out in the crosswalk and narrative.
- Where we reference runtime logs or syslog evidence, we provided sample log snippets rather than full production logs to avoid PII exposure. Full evidence can be provided under an NDA or via secure share if required.
- The diagram highlights our automatic KV cache isolation and the network egress policing implemented via per-pool NAT and proxy.

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink
HubSpot record: contact/ACME-0921

If you need a short attestation statement for the SOC 2 binder I can provide it — suggested language included below. Please confirm receipt and any follow-ups by Jan 5.

Suggested attestation (sample):
"Redwood Inference attests that the architecture described in the attached documents was in place for Dedicated and Private deployments as of December 2026. Where customer-managed components are used (e.g., customer KMS for Private deployments), Redwood documents the responsibility split and does not have direct access to customer key material unless explicitly provisioned by the customer."

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Grace —

Received the package, thank you. Initial review looks good; a couple quick clarifications before I mark it final for our binder:
1) For Dedicated — can you confirm whether cross-account peering uses AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) or standard peering? We need the specific mechanism to reference in our SIG mapping.
2) For Private air-gapped option — can you confirm the offline transfer procedure and whether transfer logs are retained for 90 days by default?

If you can respond to those two items by Jan 5 we should be able to include this in our January attestation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Information Security Lead, Acme Financial
